title: Fix Windows closed-pipe errors in Git source-pin fallback
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

When the Git `--batch -z` probe exits before its first stdin write on native Windows, CPython can raise `OSError(EINVAL)` at flush and again at close. The current reader handles only `BrokenPipeError`, so the older-Git fallback aborts before reading any pinned source.

Recognize this closed-stdin error **only on Windows**, at the request and cleanup boundaries. The existing first-request/no-response/exit-129 retry gate, exact blob validation and one-pass iterator remain intact. Other errors still propagate, and a failed legacy reader cannot trigger a third process.

Three files: the small reader fix, six behavioral tests, and a [source/evidence note](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/de93ebd044d0b00a8647a9f47f86939a6b18b9aa/docs/research/windows-git-batch-pipe-errors.md). Tooling only; no changed source pins, frozen packages, selected frontier or new κ.

## Task and overlap

- Base/current canonical main: `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`, priority revision 7.
- Publication head: `de93ebd044d0b00a8647a9f47f86939a6b18b9aa`.
- `portable-replay`, **scope changed** from regenerated-payload comparison to a reproduced platform failure in immutable-source verification. Picker seed and bounded question/stop rule are in the note.
- [Canonical claim and handoff: Discussion #4681](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4681).
- Builds on Nick Petalas's merged #2752, head `73406fd73ebaf8361b51674fad5e0b02a26db075`, which explicitly left Windows untested.
- Refreshed overlap: 450 open PRs, 3,612 Discussion records, plus all 5,860 tracked in-scope local notes. Exact error/path searches found no competing repair. Arbitrary diffs, closed remote PRs and unpublished work remain outside that coverage.
- #4579/#4679 repair exporter fixtures; the active Windows isolated-test lifetime claim in #1472 concerns a different launcher.

## Validation

**Before:** the unchanged native compatibility module reports eight passes, one error and one existing CR/LF-path skip. Its exited-child test produces the real Windows errno-22 failure. The final six new tests against an exact copy of the base reader produce eight error subcases.

**After, with `-W error -B`, both ordinary and optimized `-O` runs:**

| Environment | Scope | Result per mode |
|---|---|---|
| Windows / CPython 3.12.0 / Git 2.47.1.windows.1 | Git batch, compatibility, new pipe errors, replacement refs, committed bytes, source history | 51 passed, one existing CR/LF-path skip |
| Ubuntu under WSL / CPython 3.12.3 / Git 2.43.0 | Git batch, compatibility, new pipe errors | 23 passed, no skips |

The unchanged registered compatibility hook also passes metadata/pins and all **38** currently discovered Git-reader tests on Linux:

```sh
python3 -W error -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/git-batch-compatibility
```

The new tests cover write/flush/close errors, binary/empty/duplicate blobs, independent object IDs, single iterator consumption, closed streams and reaped children. EIO, POSIX EINVAL, exit 0/7, post-response failure and legacy-reader failure remain rejecting controls. Only option rejection and the injected error variants are simulated; real Git supplies successful fallback bytes. `git diff --check` passes.

The shared-control planner selects all **2,480** registered packages. Its policy is unchanged; those broader scientific replays were not run locally. An initial broader Windows onboarding run hit existing fixture errors and was stopped; the sparse selected baseline also lacked its complete input closure. No complete onboarding, selected cold replay or hosted CI pass is claimed.

## Credit

Nick Petalas (#2752) supplied the fallback and original tests; Douglas Colkitt the runner contracts; Arham Tahir the NUL pin batching; Woklerx the streamed-reader and cleanup lineage. Maxime Fleury's reproducibility work and the original P104/Abhinav Ramachandran reports retain their credit.

Prepared for Mihir Srivastava with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, one agent. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Run the three reader modules against an actual older Git for Windows in a disposable fixture. That binary is not installed here; this repair uses the predecessor's controlled unsupported-option probe. Synchronous pipe-read deadlines and arbitrary Git/Python-version support remain separate obligations.
